text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: This paper presents a GIS-based land use modeling study applied explicitly at the national scale of the Netherlands. It focuses primarily on land use prediction/simulation with a central research question on residential construction and land use changes under multiple future scenarios (Divided Europe, European Coordination, Global Competition). The Land Use Scanner model integrates sectoral projections and spatial suitability to generate mapped land use projections for the entire country for the year 2020. The paper quantitatively analyzes changes in residential land use (1980–1995), estimates suitability parameters, and simulates future land use patterns under multiple scenarios with spatially explicit outputs. It also links land use predictions to environmental indicator assessments. The study meets all core inclusion criteria: explicit national-scale spatial implementation, primary focus on LULC prediction, use of ≥2 quantitative future scenarios, spatially explicit modeling with outputs including mapped projections. It does not meet any exclusion criteria. Therefore, it is classified as OK.)
